note: Mutations of `vpcm_create`, `vpcm_delete`, `dp_vpcm_init` and the `vpcm_op` table, caught by build/test/t_vpcmdp.  `vpcm_run` lives in the same file and is test/mutations/vpcmrun.json's; nothing here touches it.

THREE STORES IN THIS FUNCTION CANNOT BE MUTATED AT ALL, and that is a property of the object rather than a gap in the test: `s->status = 0`, `s->mode = VPCM_MODE_IDLE` and `s->stall = 0` write zero into a block that `sysdep_memset(s, 0, sizeof(struct vpcm_root))` cleared three lines earlier, so deleting any of them changes nothing any differential test can observe.  They are registered below as `equivalent` with the memset as the proof, which is the honest record; deleting them from the source would ALSO be a behaviour-preserving change and is not proposed, because the object has three separate stores at 0x3a9c, 0x3aa3 and 0x3aaa after its memset and the source says so.

why: THE TWO STORES TOUCH DISJOINT BITS AND NEITHER READS THE OTHER'S.  The second clears bit 5 and leaves the rest; the first writes bit 4 from the LOCAL `qcFlags`, which was computed from the ORIGINAL byte before either store, and preserves every other bit through `& 0xef`.  So in either order the result is (original & 0xcf) | (kept << 4): bit 4 from the local, bit 5 zero, the other six as they were.  It is an ordering the object fixes -- 0x3ba4-0x3bb4 then 0x3bbf -- and which no input can distinguish, which is exactly why the ORDER is written from the disassembly and cannot be recovered from behaviour.

label: the mute counter takes the mask when the V.92 bit is SET
note: THE INVERTED `sbb`, and the reason the sweep has to drive bit 4 both ways: with one value of that bit the two readings are the same function.

label: the mute counter reads bit 5
the mute counter is half as long
the mute counter uses the local rather than re-reading the byte
why: THE RE-READ CANNOT RETURN ANYTHING ELSE, and this entry is here because it was WRITTEN AS A CATCHABLE MUTATION AND SURVIVED -- the proof was found by asking why.  The two statements above are `params->qcFlags = (params->qcFlags & 0xef) | ((qcFlags & 1) << 4)` and `params->qcFlags &= 0xdf`; the first sets bit 4 to `qcFlags & 1` and the second touches only bit 5, so at this statement `(params->qcFlags >> 4) & 1` IS `qcFlags & 1` for every input.  Nothing between the store and the read can write the block: it is reached only through `s->params`, which was set eight statements earlier and not since.  So the object's re-load at 0x3bca is a codegen-tier fact -- it says the source spells the read as a field and not as the local -- and no differential test can ever see it.
